deep.reconstruction:
Context: the previous page ends a geometric argument about a tetrahedron (pyramid) inscribed in the unit sphere. The planar triangle ABC has sides 2 sin(a/2), 2 sin(b/2), 2 sin(c/2), which are the chords of the spherical arcs a, b, c. Its double area is 4 sin(alpha) sin(b/2) sin(c/2), and the pyramid has height cos r. On the present page a faint pencil heading (mostly illegible; something like '20 ... angenommen ... Formeln') introduces four formulas for a spherical triangle with sides a, b, c and opposite angles A, B, C:
(1) cos(A/2) sin((b-c)/2) = sin((B-C)/2) sin(a/2)
(2) sin(A/2) sin((b+c)/2) = cos((B-C)/2) sin(a/2)
(3) cos(A/2) cos((b-c)/2) = sin((B+C)/2) cos(a/2)
(4) sin(A/2) cos((b+c)/2) = cos((B+C)/2) cos(a/2)
These are the four 'Gauss analogies' (Delambre or Mollweide analogies) of spherical trigonometry. No derivation is written on the page; they are simply stated. A standard derivation (mine, not on the page) runs as follows. Start from the spherical law of cosines and the sine rule. Write sin((B+C)/2) = sin(B/2)cos(C/2) + cos(B/2)sin(C/2). Substitute the half-angle expressions sin(B/2) = sqrt(sin(s-a)sin(s-c)/(sin a sin c)), cos(B/2) = sqrt(sin s sin(s-b)/(sin a sin c)), and the analogous ones for C. Dividing by cos(A/2) = sqrt(sin s sin(s-a)/(sin b sin c)) gives (sin(s-b)+sin(s-c))/sin a = cos((b-c)/2)/cos(a/2), which is formula (3). The other three follow in the same way, or by applying the polar triangle and changes of sign. Dividing the formulas pairwise yields Napier's analogies, e.g. tan((B+C)/2) = cos((b-c)/2)/cos((b+c)/2) * cot(A/2). Their likely purpose in this context is as auxiliary relations for the spherical/tetrahedral volume considerations of the preceding pages, but the page itself contains only the formulas.
errors: No mathematical errors: all four formulas as written agree with the standard Gauss/Delambre analogies.
The page states the formulas without derivation, so there are no steps to check.

results.what: Four relations between half-sums and half-differences of sides and angles of a spherical triangle
results.modern_name: Gauss's analogies (Delambre's analogies, Mollweide-type formulas for spherical triangles)
results.usually_credited_to: Delambre (1807, published in Connaissance des Temps for 1809), Mollweide (1808), Gauss (Theoria motus, 1809, art. 54); often named after Gauss

deep.surprise_reason: These are the well-known 'Gauss analogies', which Gauss published himself in Theoria motus (1809) and which bear his name. Their appearance in his notes is expected and routine.

checkable.asserts: Napier's analogy obtained as the quotient of (3) and (4) (should be ~0)

transcription_corrections: The heading line is very faint pencil; the readings '20 ... angenommen ... Formeln' are uncertain and may include a date. It should be marked as largely illegible.
The four formulas as transcribed match the image and are mathematically correct. In line 2 the right-hand factor is cos((B-C)/2) (capital letters, angles), not cos((b-c)/2).
